name: Rust
summary: Systems programming language that guarantees memory and data-race safety without a garbage collector through ownership, borrowing and lifetimes, combined with traits, algebraic data types, pattern matching and zero-cost abstractions.

level_notes.0: rustc (rust-lang/rust) is the reference implementation and de facto definition; it contains the compiler (compiler/), the standard library (library/) and the UI test suite (tests/ui). Alternative implementations: gccrs (GCC front end), mrustc (bootstrapping compiler without borrow checking), rustc_codegen_cranelift and rustc_codegen_gcc (alternative back ends); Miri is an interpreter for MIR that detects undefined behaviour.
level_notes.1: There is no ISO/ECMA standard. The Rust Reference is the official but explicitly incomplete and non-normative language reference; accepted RFCs define individual features; the Ferrocene Language Specification (FLS, adopted by the Rust project in 2025) is a specification written for compiler qualification. Formal models (RustBelt, Stacked/Tree Borrows, Oxide, MiniRust, a-mir-formality) cover parts of the language.
level_notes.2: The official book ('The Rust Programming Language'), Rust by Example and the Rustonomicon are tutorials/guides and therefore level 2; the rustc dev guide is the internals guide.
